```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, dpi = 120)
source(here::here("scripts/00_setup.R"))
```

# Purpose

Build a set of process models that can be calibrated on historical
GridMET and then driven, unchanged, by downscaled climate projections
(MACAv2-METDATA, which is bias-corrected to GridMET). This notebook asks two
questions of each model:

1. **How well does it fit held-out years?** Blocked 5-fold water-year
   cross-validation, as in notebooks 03–05.
2. **Does it hold up in a different climate?** A differential split-sample
   test (Klemeš 1986, *Hydrol. Sci. J.* 31:13): calibrate on one climatic
   extreme and test on the opposite one. A model that loses little skill
   (and, above all, little water-balance accuracy) here is a safer choice
   for projections.

**Models** (all in `wsva_models()`, `R/models.R`):

| Model | Snow | Soil / runoff | Routing | Free parameters |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| WBM + IHACRES | Jennings threshold, degree-day, one elevation | Thornthwaite-Mather bucket | 2 linear stores + loss | 8 |
| CemaNeige-GR4J | CemaNeige, 5 elevation bands | production store, exchange X2 | unit hydrograph + routing store | 6 |
| CemaNeige-GR5J | " | + exchange threshold X5 | " | 7 |
| CemaNeige-GR6J | " | " | + exponential store X6 (low flows) | 8 |
| HBV (TUWmodel) | degree-day, rain/snow ramp, snow correction, 5 bands | soil moisture with BETA curve | upper/lower stores + triangular routing | 15 |

**Held equal across models:** the same GridMET basin-mean forcing, the
same PET, the same folds, and DDS calibration on KGE (`r params$n_evals`
runs, doubled for HBV's 15 parameters).

**PET.** Computed from the meteorological variables, never taken from
GridMET's own PET product, so historical and future runs use an identical
method: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith grass reference ET from tmin, tmax, solar
radiation, humidity and wind, × the seasonal land-cover Kc
(`prepare_forcing()`, `R/forcing.R`). MACAv2-METDATA supplies every one of
these variables. Penman-Monteith is preferred over temperature-only PET for
projections because temperature-based formulas tend to overstate future
increases in evaporative demand (Milly & Dunne 2016, *Nat. Clim. Change*
6:946).

```{r paths}
out_dir <- params$out_dir %||% here::here("data", "processed", "results", "process_models")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
res_dir <- function(x) here::here("data", "processed", "results", x)

gauges <- get_test_gauges()
gauges$has_data <- file.exists(here::here("data", "processed", gauges$site_no, "daily.parquet"))
gauge_levels <- gauges$gauge_label
label_of <- function(site) factor(gauges$gauge_label[match(site, gauges$site_no)], levels = gauge_levels)

models <- wsva_models(n_layers = params$n_layers)
model_levels <- names(models)
inputs <- gauges %>%
  dplyr::filter(has_data) %>%
  dplyr::pull(site_no) %>%
  rlang::set_names() %>%
  purrr::map(read_basin_inputs)
```

## PET check: self-computed vs. GridMET's product

Our Penman-Monteith ETo should track GridMET's ETo closely (GridMET uses
the ASCE standardized form). If it does, swapping in projection forcing
changes PET only through the climate, not through the method.

```{r pet-check, fig.height = 3.5}
pet_cmp <- purrr::imap_dfr(inputs, ~ tibble::tibble(site_no = .y, ours = .x$daily$eto_mm,
                                                    gridmet = .x$daily$pet_ref_mm))
pet_cmp %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge = label_of(site_no)) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(r = cor(ours, gridmet), mean_ours = mean(ours), mean_gridmet = mean(gridmet),
                   ratio = mean_ours / mean_gridmet) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Daily ETo (mm/day): ours vs. GridMET")
```

# Calibration designs

```{r designs, fig.height = 3}
make_folds <- function(x, design) {
  if (design == "blocked") make_blocked_folds(x$daily$date, k = params$k_folds, warmup_years = 1)
  else make_climate_contrast_folds(x$daily, frac = params$contrast_frac, warmup_years = 1)
}

# Show the contrast groups at one gauge, with each group's mean climate
ex_site <- names(inputs)[1]
ex <- make_folds(inputs[[ex_site]], "contrast")
ann <- inputs[[ex_site]]$daily %>%
  dplyr::group_by(wy) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(p = sum(prcp_mm), t = mean(tmean_c))
ex %>%
  dplyr::distinct(contrast, wy, role) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(contrast = factor(contrast, levels = unique(ex$contrast))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(wy, contrast, fill = role)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(train = "#9ecae1", test = "#b02a24", warmup = "grey50", unused = "grey90")) +
  labs(x = "Water year", y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = paste("Climate-contrast folds at", label_of(ex_site))) +
  theme_minimal()

purrr::imap_dfr(inputs, function(x, site) {
  a <- x$daily %>% dplyr::group_by(wy) %>% dplyr::summarize(p = sum(prcp_mm), t = mean(tmean_c))
  make_folds(x, "contrast") %>%
    dplyr::filter(role %in% c("train", "test")) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(contrast, wy, role) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(a, by = "wy") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(contrast, role) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(p = mean(p), t = mean(t), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = role, values_from = c(p, t)) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(gauge = label_of(site), contrast,
                     `P change (%)` = 100 * (p_test / p_train - 1), `T change (C)` = t_test - t_train)
}) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Climate shift from calibration to test years in each contrast")
```

Wet/dry and warm/cool are not independent: at most gauges the warmest
years are also the most recent, so *cool → warm* and *early → late*
overlap. Precipitation contrasts (±40–100%) are far larger than the
temperature contrasts (~1–2 °C), which are smaller than end-of-century
warming under most scenarios — the test is a lower bound on how much a
model would be stressed by projections.

# Calibrate

Every (gauge, model, design) result is cached in `r out_dir` and reused
only if its settings and inputs are unchanged.

```{r run}
run_one <- function(site_no, model, design) {
  site <- site_no
  spec <- models[[model]]
  x <- inputs[[site]]
  key <- list(model = model, design = design, bounds = spec$bounds,
              n_evals = round(params$n_evals * spec$n_evals_mult), n_layers = params$n_layers,
              k_folds = params$k_folds, contrast_frac = params$contrast_frac,
              static = as.list(x$static), hypso = x$hypso)
  f <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("%s_%s_%s.rds", site, gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "", model), design))
  if (file.exists(f) && !isTRUE(params$rerun)) {
    r <- readRDS(f)
    if (isTRUE(all.equal(r$key, key))) return(r)
  }
  folds <- make_folds(x, design)
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  cv <- cross_validate_model(spec$build(x), spec$bounds, x$daily$q_mm, folds, objective = kge,
                             n_evals = key$n_evals, n_cores = params$n_cores, seed = 1)
  contrast_of <- dplyr::distinct(folds, fold, dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of("contrast")))
  r <- c(cv, list(key = key, contrasts = contrast_of,
                  minutes = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))))
  saveRDS(r, f)
  message(sprintf("%s %s %s: %.1f min", site, model, design, r$minutes))
  r
}

grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(site_no = names(inputs), model = model_levels, design = c("blocked", "contrast"))
runs <- purrr::pmap(grid, run_one)

collect <- function(part) purrr::map2_dfr(runs, seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(r, i) {
  out <- dplyr::mutate(r[[part]], site_no = grid$site_no[i], model = grid$model[i], design = grid$design[i])
  if ("contrast" %in% names(r$contrasts)) out <- dplyr::left_join(out, r$contrasts, by = "fold")
  out
})
metrics <- collect("metrics")
cv_params <- collect("params")
sims <- collect("sims")
readr::write_csv(metrics, file.path(out_dir, "metrics.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cv_params, file.path(out_dir, "params.csv"))
arrow::write_parquet(sims, file.path(out_dir, "test_sims.parquet"))

tibble::tibble(model = grid$model, design = grid$design, minutes = purrr::map_dbl(runs, "minutes")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model, design) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(minutes_per_gauge = mean(minutes), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Calibration time")
```

# Results

## Held-out years (blocked CV)

The day-of-year climatology benchmark (notebook 03) is shown for
reference; it was scored on the identical test blocks.

```{r blocked}
model_cols <- c("WBM + IHACRES" = "#1b6ca8", "CemaNeige-GR4J" = "#459a74", "CemaNeige-GR5J" = "#7fbf7b",
                "CemaNeige-GR6J" = "#1b7837", "HBV (TUWmodel)" = "#dca237",
                "DOY climatology" = "grey40")
read_ref <- function(dir, keep) {
  f <- file.path(res_dir(dir), "cv_metrics.csv")
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  readr::read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% dplyr::filter(set == "test", model %in% keep)
}
blocked <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::filter(metrics, design == "blocked", set == "test"),
  read_ref("wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith", "DOY climatology")
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no), model = factor(model, levels = names(model_cols)))

blocked %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(kge, nse, log_nse), names_to = "metric") %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, gauge, color = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = model_cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

blocked %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge, model) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(kge = median(kge), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = kge) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median test KGE over the 5 blocks")

blocked %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(c(kge, nse, log_nse), median), abs_pbias = median(abs(pbias))) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median over all gauges and blocks")
```

## Transfer to a different climate (differential split-sample)

For projections, the most important property is that the water balance
stays right when the climate shifts, so bias is shown alongside KGE.

```{r contrast}
contrast_levels <- c("wet -> dry", "dry -> wet", "cool -> warm", "warm -> cool", "early -> late")
contrast_test <- metrics %>%
  dplyr::filter(design == "contrast", set == "test") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no), model = factor(model, levels = model_levels),
                contrast = factor(contrast, levels = contrast_levels))

contrast_test %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(kge, pbias), names_to = "metric") %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, contrast, color = model)) +
  geom_vline(data = data.frame(metric = c("kge", "pbias"), x = c(NA, 0)), aes(xintercept = x), color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(gauge ~ metric, scales = "free_x", labeller = labeller(gauge = label_wrap_gen(20))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = model_cols) +
  labs(x = "KGE / percent bias (positive = under-prediction)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r robustness}
# Skill lost moving from held-out years in a similar climate (blocked CV
# median) to the opposite climate extreme, per gauge and model
blocked_med <- metrics %>%
  dplyr::filter(design == "blocked", set == "test") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site_no, model) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(kge_blocked = median(kge), .groups = "drop")
robust <- contrast_test %>%
  dplyr::left_join(blocked_med, by = c("site_no", "model")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(kge_drop = kge_blocked - kge)

robust %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(kge_contrast = median(kge), kge_drop = median(kge_drop),
                   worst_kge = min(kge), abs_pbias = median(abs(pbias)), worst_abs_pbias = max(abs(pbias))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(abs_pbias) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Climate-contrast tests: median over gauges and contrasts")

robust %>%
  dplyr::group_by(contrast, model) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(kge = median(kge), pbias = median(pbias), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = c(kge, pbias)) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "By contrast (median over gauges)")
```

## Parameter stability across climates

Parameters that move a lot between contrasts are absorbing climate
differences rather than describing the basin, which is a warning sign for
extrapolation.

```{r param-stability, fig.height = 9}
cv_params %>%
  dplyr::filter(design == "contrast") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(function(d, k) {
    b <- models[[k$model]]$bounds
    tidyr::pivot_longer(d, dplyr::all_of(b$param), names_to = "param") %>%
      dplyr::left_join(b, by = "param") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(scaled = (value - lower) / (upper - lower))
  }) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no), contrast = factor(contrast, levels = contrast_levels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(scaled, param, color = contrast)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 1) +
  facet_grid(model ~ gauge, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
             labeller = labeller(gauge = label_wrap_gen(15), model = label_wrap_gen(12))) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Position within bounds", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Hydrographs, flow duration and seasonality (blocked CV)

```{r series}
series <- sims %>%
  dplyr::filter(design == "blocked") %>%
  dplyr::select(site_no, date, model, obs, sim)
long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::distinct(series, site_no, date, q_mm = obs) %>% dplyr::mutate(series = "obs"),
  dplyr::transmute(series, site_no, date, q_mm = sim, series = model)
) %>% dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no))
series_cols <- c(obs = "black", model_cols[model_levels])
```

```{r hydrographs, fig.height = 10}
long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site_no) %>%
  dplyr::filter(date >= max(date) - 2 * 365) %>%
  ggplot(aes(date, q_mm, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = series_cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Streamflow (mm/day)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r fdc, fig.height = 6}
long %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(q_mm)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge, series) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(exceedance = 1 - (rank(q_mm, ties.method = "first") - 0.5) / dplyr::n()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(exceedance, pmax(q_mm, 1e-3), color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = series_cols) +
  labs(x = "Exceedance probability", y = "Streamflow (mm/day, log)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r seasonal, fig.height = 6}
long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge, series, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(q_mm = mean(q_mm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(month, q_mm, color = series)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = series_cols) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Mean streamflow (mm/day)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Notes

- **Next step for projections:** a MACAv2-METDATA reader that writes the
  same forcing columns (`forcing_required_vars()`), then
  `spec$build(x_future)(calibrated_params)` for each model; see the header
  of `R/models.R`.
- **Not included in standard Penman-Monteith:** the CO2 effect on stomatal
  resistance, which reduces transpiration under elevated CO2 and can
  noticeably lower projected PET (Yang et al. 2019, *Nat. Clim. Change*
  9:44). A candidate option for the projection runs.
- **Kc is fixed** at the current land cover; vegetation change is not
  represented.
